headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Great Expectations file I/O into a knowledge-management pair; prompt injection and capability conflict are otherwise limited by no-network, docs-only profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, while great_expectations reads files and produces validation results. A direct injection path is not documented, but if outputs from awesome-selfhosted are manually copied into GE inputs, malformed content could influence validation workflows. The pair lacks a shared channel in the profiles, so this stays low.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are manually pasted into agent_b file inputs or docs fields
IF agent_b treats copied text as trusted configuration or test content
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b config files
Review pasted content before running validations
Use a separate scratch file for transfers
Add a short provenance note to copied snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches files containing data sources, validation results, and documentation, while agent_a is a knowledge-management artifact with no declared data classes. If both are used in a shared workspace, GE can expose file contents in validation outputs or docs, creating a plausible leakage path. The profiles do not show encryption or isolation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same workspace or filesystem
IF agent_b processes sensitive data sources or validation results in that workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Restrict GE runs to non-sensitive sample files
Store validation outputs in a dedicated folder
Delete temporary docs after runs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network capabilities in the profile, while agent_b can install packages but has no declared filesystem write beyond file surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or locking issues, so a write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because agent_b's full write scope is not specified, so low is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory
IF agent_b writes validation artifacts into files that agent_a also edits externally
mitigations: Use read-only inputs for agent_a
Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Document ownership of each workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations can turn file contents into validation results and documentation, so if agent_a's curated content is fed into agent_b, GE may render it as authoritative without an explicit verification step. agent_a itself is not an action-taking agent, which limits blast radius, but the handoff can still propagate errors into downstream reports. The interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a-generated text is used as input to agent_b validation or documentation
IF agent_b publishes validation results without human review
mitigations: Require human review of GE outputs
Label imported text as untrusted
Cross-check key claims against source files
Keep generated docs separate from source data

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no secrets handled or regulated data classes. agent_b touches documentation and validation results, but there is no evidence of residency, retention, or certification mismatch, and agent_a has no data classes touched. Compliance risk is therefore limited to documentation hygiene rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b's validation inputs
IF documentation or validation outputs are retained beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in test runs
Set a short retention window for outputs
Review docs for accidental sensitive content
Record the data class used in each run
